name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Monday 26 December 1983

clue.text: Friend's return stroke is made in a careless way

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the friend's word is read from its end

blocks.note: a pal is a friend; the 's is read as a plural S
a dash is a stroke of the pen

explanation.surface: A friend's tennis return is hit sloppily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return stroke' reads as one tennis phrase, but 'return' only turns the friend round and 'stroke' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash describes work done hastily and carelessly, the adjective matching 'made in a careless way'.

clue.text: Is inclined to be shiftless, as it were, about work

definitions.text: to be shiftless, as it were, about work

blocks.note: first meaning: lies at an angle

blocks.clueFragment: to be shiftless, as it were, about work
blocks.note: second meaning: idles or sneaks off to avoid work, as in the slang phrase 'off'

explanation.walkthrough: To 'slope off' or 'slope about' is British slang for sloping away from duty, idling lazily.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both leans at an angle and, in slang, loafs or sneaks away from work.

clue.text: Bill takes money - caused by stress

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, the emphasis that stress produces, while the clue words read as a description

blocks.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a cent is a small coin; 'takes' just joins it on

explanation.surface: A demand for payment collects cash and causes anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stress' suggests worry, but it is the stress laid on a syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent is the prominence on a syllable produced by stressing it in speech.

clue.text: Rides badly - has to pull up - take no notice

indicators.note: something done badly is muddled, so these letters are put out of order
in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written before it is jumbled
to drag is to pull

explanation.surface: A poor horseman has to rein in, ignoring everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull up' looks like reining in a horse; here 'up' turns the word for pull round.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard something is to ignore it, the same verb sense as 'take no notice'.

clue.text: Weapon Barney Wood designed, in a way

indicators.note: something designed is newly arranged, so these letters are put in a fresh order
in says the rearranged letters sit inside the word that follows

blocks.note: ST, street, is a way; its two letters split to wrap round
taken as written before it is jumbled

explanation.surface: A craftsman called Barney Wood made a weapon, after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' reads as a hedge meaning 'sort of'; it is an instruction to put the jumble inside ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword-bayonet is a long bladed bayonet that can also be used as a sword, so it is a weapon.

clue.text: Good sorts of builders?

blocks.note: the surface reading: reliable, decent people, a slang word for whom is the answer
the setter's reading: the clay blocks a builder lays in walls

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a 'brick' is a thoroughly decent, dependable person; the question mark flags the builder's literal sense of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun means both dependable people (old slang) and the building blocks used by bricklayers.

clue.text: Where ships might be . found by the island, say

indicators.note: say means as spoken, so the island's name is matched by its sound

blocks.note: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean

explanation.surface: Ships could be anchored near an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop is a scanning slip in the newspaper text. Roads (a roadstead) is sheltered water outside a harbour where ships anchor.
explanation.definitionFit: Roads, or a roadstead, is a sheltered anchorage near shore, a place where ships lie at anchor.

clue.text: Dismisses employees?

blocks.note: first meaning: discharges from service, especially an officer in disgrace
second meaning: staff who handle the cash in a bank or shop

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a boss firing staff; the same word is the verb for discharging and the plural noun for till staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier is to dismiss from the armed forces in disgrace; cashiers are also cash-handling staff.

clue.text: Yachtsmen not going to use this rig?

definitions.text: Yachtsmen not going to use this rig?

blocks.note: the surface reading: sailors who are not setting out at all
the setter's reading: sailors who will 'not go', i.e. stay, would rig the sail named after a stay

explanation.walkthrough: A stay is a rope bracing a mast, and the sail set on one is named after it; 'not going' is to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: A staysail is a triangular sail hoisted on a stay, part of a yacht's rig.

clue.text: In this event, no-one's to account to leader for retreat

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, an event; the clue's phrase is the setting 'on this occasion' that the noun completes

indicators.note: a retreat moves backwards, so the whole string built from the earlier words is read from its end

blocks.note: NO, then I for one, then the 'S
ACC is the standard abbreviation of account
the final letter of the string; the printed words give it only loosely

explanation.surface: Nobody is to answer to the commander for the withdrawal during this event.
explanation.walkthrough: NO + I + S + ACC + O, read backwards, spells OCCASION. The O at the end is not cleanly supplied by the clue as printed (scanned newspaper text), so treat that letter as the crossings' gift.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasion is a particular event or time, as in 'on this occasion'.

clue.text: A UN blunder - main cause of ill-feeling

definitions.note: nausea is the ill-feeling itself rather than its cause; the setter stretches it for the surface

indicators.note: a blunder is a bungled mess, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the main is an old word for the open sea

explanation.surface: A United Nations gaffe is the chief source of bad blood between countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main cause' looks like one phrase meaning chief reason, but 'main' is the sea and the definition is the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is sickness in the stomach, a literal ill feeling; the setter makes it the cause of one.

clue.text: Very little passenger transport

blocks.note: the surface reading: scarcely any public transport running
the setter's reading: a carriage for a very little passenger, a baby

explanation.walkthrough: 'Very little' seems to mean scarcely any, but it describes the size of the passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: A perambulator, or pram, is a pushed carriage in which a baby, a very little passenger, rides.

clue.text: The bondsman?

blocks.note: the surface reading: a man in bondage, a serf, or one who stands surety
the setter's reading: the 'man' who deals with Britain's Premium Bonds by picking the winning numbers

explanation.walkthrough: Premium Bonds are a British government savings scheme paying prizes by lottery; the winning numbers are drawn by a machine with a man's name, an acronym for Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: ERNIE is the random-number machine that selects Premium Bond prize winners, so it is the bonds' man in a punning sense.

clue.text: Reid's set's awkward in formal wear

indicators.note: awkward things sit badly, so these letters are set in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophes

explanation.surface: Somebody named Reid looks uncomfortable in his evening clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress ties are the bow ties worn with dinner jackets and tails, an example of formal wear.

clue.text: Vehicles are returning to one sort of inn

indicators.note: something returning heads back, so the word are is read from its end

blocks.note: caravans are towed vehicles
taken as written before it turns
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Coaches head back to a particular kind of hostelry.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the eastern roadside inn where caravans of travellers stopped overnight, so 'Vehicles' fits both the wordplay and the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravanserai is a large inn with a courtyard on desert trade routes, a particular kind of inn.

clue.text: Wonder what the bull might do?

blocks.note: first meaning: ponder or guess
second meaning: a stock-market bull buys shares hoping prices rise

explanation.walkthrough: The bull is not the farm animal but a stock-market investor betting on a rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To speculate is to conjecture, and also to invest riskily in hope of profit, as market bulls do.

clue.text: The skipper's mistake, per . haps

blocks.note: the surface reading: an error by a ship's captain
the setter's reading: the error of one who skips, leaving something out; the stray dot is a scanning slip

explanation.walkthrough: 'Skipper' looks like a captain; here it is anyone who skips something, and leaving something out is the fault.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is something left out, the typical slip of a person who skips over things.

clue.text: Formerly yielded about a quarter, and that's surpassed

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the yielding word goes round the quarter

blocks.note: ex- means former
to cede is to yield or give up
east is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: Someone once gave up roughly a quarter, and that was beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: A quarter is a compass point here (N, E, S or W), not a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Exceeded means went beyond, a past-tense synonym of surpassed.

clue.text: In "which people serve drinks, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: a tennis event for pairs of a man and a woman, in which players serve
second meaning: double measures of spirits blended with something

explanation.walkthrough: The stray quotation mark is a scanning slip in the newspaper text and means nothing. 'Serve drinks' reads as bar work, but 'serve' belongs with the tennis meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the tennis event for mixed-sex pairs and could describe large mixed spirits measures.

clue.text: Avoid holding up attempt to find and eastern ruler

indicators.note: holding means grasping inside, so the avoid word wraps round the next piece
in a down entry, up means the attempt word is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: to shun is to avoid
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: Steer clear of delaying the effort to locate an Oriental monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding up' reads as delaying, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A shogun was a hereditary military ruler of Japan, so an eastern ruler.

clue.text: Cases of car repairs getting put up

definitions.text: Cases of car repairs getting put up

blocks.note: the surface reading: instances of garage work; the setter's: wooden packing boxes

blocks.clueFragment: of car repairs getting put up
blocks.note: the setter's reading: old cars needing repairs are slang 'boxes' too, and goods put up for shipping go in such cases

explanation.walkthrough: Crate is slang for a battered old car, and crates are the boxes goods are packed in; the clue plays on both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Crates are wooden packing cases, and the singular is also slang for a ramshackle old car.

clue.text: In a short time, weed bursts into flower

indicators.note: something that bursts breaks apart, so the letters of the weed come out scrambled
into says the scrambled letters go inside the short time

blocks.note: a spell is a short period of time
taken as written before it is jumbled

explanation.surface: A weed quickly bursts into bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bursts into flower' reads as one phrase about blooming; 'flower' alone is the definition. 'In a short time' looks like an adverb but supplies a noun for the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is a small blue-flowered plant, Veronica, so it is an example of a flower.

clue.text: Poet has finished speaking

indicators.note: speaking means as heard out loud, so the word for finished is matched by its sound

blocks.note: done means finished

explanation.walkthrough: John Donne was the 17th-century English metaphysical poet; his name is said like the word for finished.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne is a famous English poet, so the surname names a poet.

clue.text: American female teacher

blocks.note: US abbreviates the United States
her is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman who teaches in America.
explanation.walkthrough: An usher was once an assistant schoolmaster, an old sense the setter relies on.
explanation.definitionFit: Usher is an archaic word for an under-master or assistant teacher at a school.

clue.text: Element that surrounding a god

indicators.note: surrounding means the first piece goes round the outside of the next

blocks.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, 'that is'
Odin is the chief Norse god

explanation.surface: A chemical element that encloses a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That' = IE is a crossword convention from the abbreviation i.e. ('that is').
explanation.definitionFit: Iodine is a chemical element, the halogen with symbol I.

clue.text: Frank's flat?

blocks.note: first meaning: honest and direct, without evasion
second meaning: level and without curves, as a line or a stretch of course

explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name owning a flat (an apartment); both words are adjectives with a shared synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means honest and plain-spoken, and also level or without bends.

clue.text: Signified assent prior to retirement?

blocks.note: first meaning: moved the head up and down to say yes
second meaning: dozed off with the head drooping, as before going to bed

explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here means going to bed, not leaving work; one 'nods off' just before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both the yes gesture of the head and the drooping head of someone falling asleep.

clue.text: RN needs a replacement for world war battle area

indicators.note: a replacement puts things in new places, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; it also serves in the indicator phrase

explanation.surface: The Royal Navy needs a fresh man for a wartime battle zone.
explanation.walkthrough: RN is the Royal Navy. The forested region of Belgium and Luxembourg saw major fighting in both world wars, including the Battle of the Bulge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ardennes was a battleground in both world wars, so it is a world war battle area.
